entry_points.name: close_account
entry_points.note: Sets User.deleted_at to the current time and commits; the module is registered in app.py ROUTES.

stores.name: users

fields.name: deleted_at
fields.note: The column the close_account route writes and the purge job filters on.

erasure.note: close_account only stamps deleted_at; the row is removed by purge_closed_accounts, which deletes users whose deleted_at is older than RETENTION_DAYS and is scheduled daily at 04:00 in CELERYBEAT_SCHEDULE.

stores.note: Table holding the account holder record.

stores.name: invoices

fields.name: reference
fields.note: Invoice reference; the inline comment says the row is kept for the statutory accounting period and that the purge job does not touch this table.

erasure.note: The User.invoices relationship carries no cascade= string, so the ORM delete of the user does not propagate; the only deletion path is the database-level ondelete="CASCADE" on user_id, and the repository uses a SQLite URL with no PRAGMA foreign_keys=ON listener, so it does not show foreign keys are enforced.

stores.note: Table of invoices carrying a user_id foreign key to users.

stores.name: nightly_backup

fields.name: email
fields.note: Column copied out of the users table into the dump by DUMP_COLUMNS.

fields.name: full_name
fields.note: Column copied out of the users table into the dump by DUMP_COLUMNS.

fields.name: reference
fields.note: Column copied out of the invoices table into the dump by DUMP_COLUMNS.

erasure.note: dump_database writes the rows to nightly_backup.json; the file carries a SCHEDULE cron string and a BACKUP_RETENTION_DAYS constant of 35, and no function in the repository reads that constant or removes the file.

stores.note: JSON file written by dump_database from the users and invoices tables.

retention.criteria: kept for the statutory accounting period; the purge job does not touch this table
